assessment.nobel_worthiness: Aberration correction of electron lenses overturned Scherzer's 1936 theorem as a practical limit and made routine sub-angstrom imaging and spectroscopy possible. It is an invention with a clear, specific technical identity, and its impact is broad across physics, materials science and chemistry: atomic-column imaging of interfaces, defects and oxides is now standard. That fits a 'discovery or invention' criterion well. I work in this field and so judge the instrumental consequences with close familiarity, and I note that closeness explicitly.
assessment.attribution: The decisive roles are well separated: Rose supplied the corrector theory and design, Haider led the hexapole corrector realisation for the TEM, and Urban led the demonstration and application to materials-level imaging. All three credited names correspond to this core triad, so a fair configuration is supported. Other groups (e.g. scanning-transmission correctors) contributed in parallel and could be raised as a boundary question.
assessment.maturity: Commercial and widespread use for over two decades, with independent confirmation by many groups and a mature, stable interpretation. Recognition is timely to slightly overdue.
uncertainties: Whether the prize should also reflect the parallel STEM-corrector development by other groups is a boundary-of-credit question I cannot settle from the supplied text.
As a microscopist I may overweight the importance of instrumentation; I have not independently verified the exact attribution of each design step.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal, reached fractional uncertainties near 1e-18 and now underpins tests of fundamental constants, relativistic geodesy and the prospect of redefining the second. It is a clear invention with outstanding precision-measurement impact.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and first realised it; Ye's group drove the strontium clocks to record performance and the broader program. Two names make a clean configuration, though trapped-ion and other clock pioneers may be seen as adjacent and Hall and Haensch were already honoured for the comb.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent labs have reproduced and surpassed the early performance; the technology is mature though redefinition of the second is still pending, so recognition is timely but not forced.
uncertainties: The relative share between the concept (Katori) and performance leadership (Ye) could be debated.
I rely on general knowledge for the exact chronology of first lattice-clock demonstrations.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Theory predicting flat bands at magic twist angles, followed by observation of correlated insulating and superconducting states in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene, opened a new platform of tunable correlated quantum matter. The originality is high and the field is large, with moire engineering extending to other materials.
assessment.attribution: The theory-experiment pairing is natural: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the quantitative flat-band prediction, and Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive experimental observations. Other experimental and theoretical contributors, and the role of sample-quality advances, complicate a three-way split but the supplied names are a defensible configuration.
assessment.maturity: Strong independent replication across groups, but the interpretation of superconductivity and correlated states remains actively contested and the field is still moving rapidly, so recognition may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: The microscopic mechanism of superconductivity is unsettled.
Sample-dependent behaviour and twist-angle disorder remain open issues.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit quantum electrodynamics created strong coupling between superconducting qubits and microwave resonators with a controlled architecture, which is the basis of dispersive readout and much of today's superconducting quantum processors. The conceptual clarity and downstream impact are considerable.
assessment.attribution: Blais and collaborators supplied the theoretical proposal, Wallraff and Schoelkopf the first experimental demonstration. This is a clean theory-experiment division. The earlier 2025 recognition of superconducting-circuit macroscopic quantum effects overlaps in subject and raises a proximity question; it is also hard to separate cQED from the transmon and related inventions.
assessment.maturity: Widely confirmed and mature in practice, but timing could be judged close to a recently honoured area.
uncertainties: Overlap with recent prize recognition in superconducting circuits is a concern for novelty of the topic.
Whether the transmon and qubit-design contributions need separate attribution is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum spin Hall effect and topological insulators gave a new classification of matter through protected edge and surface states, with strong theoretical depth and clear experimental signatures in HgTe wells.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the original theoretical prediction; Molenkamp led the first experimental observation. Other important contributors (e.g. the HgTe prediction and 3D topological insulator work) are not in the credited names, so the configuration leaves out significant parts of the field. The 2016 prize on topological phases partly overlaps.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed and mature, with some practical applications still limited; overlap with 2016 makes timing less compelling.
uncertainties: Credit for the HgTe prediction and for three-dimensional topological insulators sits outside the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Giant tunnel magnetoresistance in crystalline MgO barriers, predicted from coherent spin-dependent tunnelling and then realised, made large room-temperature signals possible and underlies read heads and magnetic memory. It is an interface-physics result that I find convincing, since the atomic structure of the junction interface determines the effect.
assessment.attribution: Butler's calculations supplied the theoretical basis; Parkin and Yuasa independently demonstrated large effects in 2004. A three-way configuration is supported, although others also contributed and giant magnetoresistance was already recognised in 2007, so a prize may be seen as an extension.
assessment.maturity: Strong confirmation and large technology impact, long mature; the physics-prize novelty relative to 2007 is the main question.
uncertainties: Fine allocation of credit between independent experimental groups.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum simulation of Hubbard models with ultracold atoms in optical lattices realised strongly correlated many-body physics in an adjustable setting, with the Mott insulator transition as a landmark and later work on Fermi-Hubbard physics and single-site imaging.
assessment.attribution: Zoller supplied key proposals, Greiner and Bloch landmark experiments, and Esslinger important fermionic results. Only three names can be chosen, which excludes someone with a strong claim; the ideal configuration is uncertain. Jaksch is not credited, though the Bose-Hubbard proposal is usually associated with him.
assessment.maturity: Large, mature field with independent confirmation; the main open issue is whether quantitative new physics beyond existing methods has been delivered.
uncertainties: The original proposal credit is not fully represented in the supplied names.
Overlap with the related candidate on controlled atoms.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery of fast radio bursts, an unexpected population of extragalactic millisecond radio transients, opened a new area; the Lorimer burst was a clear, original discovery with large follow-up impact through localisation and cosmological-probe potential.
assessment.attribution: The initial detection is clearly credited to Lorimer, Bailes and collaborators, with McLaughlin as co-discoverer in the same paper; the three-name limit excludes someone with a real claim. Later localisation and repeaters were by other groups.
assessment.maturity: Population is well confirmed, but physical origins are still not resolved, so the interpretation is not stable and recognition may be early.
uncertainties: Progenitor and emission mechanism remain unknown.
Choice between McLaughlin and Bailes for the third place is not obvious.
